paite: Huchiin Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
english: Then Job answered,

paite: Aw ka lungjinna kibuk peuhmah leh, huan ka tuahsiatna khaina ah kikoih khawm peuhmah leh:
english: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

paite: Tuin tuipitea piaunel sangin a gikzo ding: huaijiakin ka thute leng a huham hi.
english: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.

paite: Thilbangkimhihthei thalte lah ka sungah a om ngala, gu huai akipana ka khain a dawn vek: Pathian mulkimhuainate kei dou dingin a kivual petmah uhi.
english: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

paite: Loupa a neih laiin gam sabengtung a ham hia? ahihkeileh a annekding tungah bawngtal a ham hia?
english: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

paite: Gim neilou chi tel louin a kine thei dia hia? ahihkeileh aktuida ah limna mawngmawng a om hia?
english: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

paite: Ka khain amaute a khoih nuam kei; kei dingin an kihhuai bang ahi uh.
english: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

paite: Aw ka nget tang thei leng jaw; ka thil deih Pathianin honphal lejaw:
english: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

paite: Kei honhihgawp dingin Pathian deihlam hi lai henla; a khut zanin, kei honsat khe mai leh:
english: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

paite: Huchiin lungmuanna ka nei lai mai dia; ahi, dawmlou natna ah ka kipak ding: Mi Siangthou thute lah ka kitheihmohbawl ngal kei a.
english: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

paite: Ka hatna bang ahia, ka ngak ding? huan ka beina bang ahia, ka kuhkal ding?
english: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

paite: Ka hatna, suangte hatna hi hia? ahihkeileh ka sa dalsik hia?
english: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

paite: Keiah panpihna a om het kei hilou hia, huan kei akipan theihsiamna hawlmangin?
english: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?

paite: Bah dia mansaa om kiangah a lawmin Siamna a etsak ding ahi kei mo; huchilou-in Bangkimhihthei kihtakna a tawpsan ahi kei ding mo.
english: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

paite: Luita bangin ka unaute a lepchiah uh; luita mangthang luanna bangin.
english: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

paite: Huai tuh tuikhalin a voma; huai ah vuk a kisel.
english: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

paite: A lum hun chiangin a tuimang ua, a sat chingin a mun ua kipan a mangthang uh.
english: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

paite: Huai lampia khualzinte a pial ua, bangmah omlouhna munah a paitou ua, a mangthang uh.
english: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.

paite: Tema khualzinten a zong ua, Seba pawlten a lamen uh.
english: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

paite: A kilamet hangun a zahlak uh; huai lamah avapai ua a hawmsuak uh.
english: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

paite: Tuin lah bangmah na hi ngal kei ua; mulkimhuaina na mu ua, na lau uhi.
english: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

paite: Kei honpia un? ahihkeileh na neihlehlam ua kipanin kei adingin thilpiak lan un, ka chi hia?
english: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’

paite: Ahihkeileh, nuaisiahhatmite khut ahipan hontan un, ka chi hia?
english: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’

paite: Hon sinsakin, huan ka dai ding: ka lamhaihna theisiam dingin hon bawlin.
english: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

paite: Dikna thute hat hina mahmah e: Himahleh na miselnain bang a selphoua?
english: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

paite: Thute selphou dinga um na hi uh hia? Chimoh mi thugente huih bang ahi chih theiin.
english: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

paite: A hi, paneiloute tungah ai na san ding ua, na lawm uh sumsinna vanin na bawl ding uh.
english: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

paite: Tuin huaijiakin hehpihtakin hon en un; na ma uah ka juau ka gen sin ngal kei a.
english: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.

paite: Kik nawn un ka honngen ahi, diklouhna om kei hen; ahi, kik nawn un, ka thu a dik ahi.Ka lei ah diklouhna a om hia? thil hoihlou ka leiin a theikak theikei dia hia?
english: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

paite: Ka lei ah diklouhna a om hia? thil hoihlou ka leiin a theikak theikei dia hia?
english: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
